name: Margaret Rose
heroAlt: Margaret Rose standing in a rose garden in warm evening light
tributeHtml:
Her kindness was her legacy.
Her love lives on.
shareDescription: A personal memorial song created from her story.
lyrics:
She loved the soil upon her hands
And sunlight in her hair
She grew roses in her garden
And left her kindness there

She knew the names of every child
Who passed her classroom door
And somehow made the quiet ones
Believe a little more

She kept a tin of buttons
And letters tied with string
Birthday cards from years gone by
And every precious thing

Margaret Rose, we’re missing you
And all the love you gave
In gardens full of morning sun
In every heart you shaped
You gave us words, you gave us grace
You taught us how to care
And when the roses bloom again
We’ll feel you standing there

She made a home where tea was poured
And cake was always near
Where every guest was welcomed in
With “come on in, my dear”
She loved the spring and Sunday roast
The books beside her bed
The stories read to bright young eyes
The little prayers she said

And though we wish for one more cup
One more “come in, my dear”
The love she gave so freely
Is still living with us here

Margaret Rose, we’re missing you
And all the love you gave
In gardens full of morning sun
In every heart you shaped
You gave us words, you gave us grace
You taught us how to care
And when the roses bloom again
We’ll feel you standing there

So rest now, gentle Margaret
Your work on earth is done
The seeds you planted long ago
Are reaching for the sun
rememberingParagraphs: Margaret was a beloved teacher, gardener and friend whose kindness touched everyone she met.
She found joy in simple things — roses opening in the morning, a good book beside her bed, and time spent with the people she loved.
storyParagraphs: Margaret Rose was born in 1946 and grew up in a home where things were cared for, mended and kept. From an early age she loved books, flowers and the quiet satisfaction of helping something grow. Those small pleasures stayed with her throughout her life.

She became a primary school teacher and was remembered for noticing the children who might otherwise have gone unseen. Margaret had a gentle way of encouraging the shy ones, calming the worried ones and helping every child believe they had something worthwhile to offer.

Outside the classroom, her garden was her favourite place. She knew which roses needed patience, which corners caught the best morning sun and when to leave the seed heads for the birds. Friends rarely left without a cutting, a small bunch of flowers or a promise that she would save them some seeds.

Her home carried the same warmth. Tea was poured generously, cake was usually close at hand and visitors were welcomed without ceremony. Margaret kept birthday cards, letters, buttons and little objects that held a memory, because she understood that ordinary things can become precious when they are connected to someone we love.

Margaret’s life was not loud, but it was deeply felt. Her kindness lived in classrooms, gardens, cups of tea, remembered birthdays and the confidence she quietly planted in other people. Like the roses she tended, the care she gave continues to bloom in the lives she touched.
